en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Garlic 8.
The Training Rule on Disposing of Excrement.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

Now at that time, a certain brahmin who had finished his royal service, thinking, "I shall seek out that very same path for my service," washed his head and was walking from the royal palace toward the nuns' quarters.
A certain nun, having defecated in a basin, threw it over the wall; it struck the top of that brahmin's head.
Then that brahmin complained, grumbled, and became indignant:
“These women are no longer ascetics; they are shaven-headed harlots.
How indeed can they carry a vessel of excrement on their heads?
I shall burn down their dwelling.”
Taking a torch, he entered the dwelling.
A certain lay follower, coming out from the dwelling, saw that brahmin entering the dwelling with a torch.
Having seen him, he said this to the brahmin:
“Sir, why do you enter this dwelling with a torch?
“Sir, these shaven-headed harlots have struck me on the head with a bowl of excrement.
I shall burn down their dwelling.”
“Go, O brahmin; this is auspicious.
You shall receive a thousand [pieces of gold] and that soldier’s path.
Then that brahmin, having washed his head, went to the royal palace and received the thousand and that soldier’s path.
Then that lay follower entered the dwelling, informed the bhikkhunīs of this matter, and rebuked them.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as before] ...were indignant, disparaged [the act], and complained:
"How can these bhikkhunīs discard excrement over a wall?"... [as before] ...
“Is it true, monks, that nuns are indeed throwing excrement over a wall?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... [as before]...
"How indeed, monks, could bhikkhunīs discard excrement over a wall?
This, monks, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of the faith of those who have it...

And so, monks, let the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule: "Whatever bhikkhunī should discard excrement over a wall, there is an offense of wrong-doing."* (*The full rule includes the penalty of pācittiya.)
“Whatever nun should throw away or cause to be thrown away feces, urine, rubbish, or food scraps over a wall or over a rampart, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Whatever nun” means whichever nun of such a kind... [and so forth].
"Bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Uccāra" (excrement) means:
"Excrement" is what is meant.
"Urine" is what is meant by "urine."
"Refuse" (saṅkāra) means rubbish;
"remnants" (vighāsa) means—
Or moving bones, or bones, or used water.
A wall means three kinds of walls: a brick wall, a stone wall, and a wooden wall.
"A rampart" means three kinds of ramparts: a brick rampart, a stone rampart, and a wooden rampart.
"Beyond the wall" means...
Beyond the wall.
Beyond the enclosure wall means on the far side of the enclosure wall.
"Should discard" means she discards it herself; there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Should cause to be discarded" means...
If she instructs another, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
If, having been instructed once, she discards even a large amount, there is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*).
There is no offense—
Having looked [at it], she discards it;
she discards it in a place free from grass;
[this applies to] one who is insane.
"By one who is a first offender.
The eighth training rule is concluded.
